correctness.rationale: For n>=3, h>0 the upper/lower bases and three adjacent side facets give exactly four active facet normals per vertex: (0,0,+1), (e_j,-k), (c e_j +/-q t_j,+k) on top, with vertical signs reversed below; k=(1-c)/(2h), c=cos(pi/n), q=sin(pi/n). An illuminating direction at the upper base requires negative vertical component and the lower base requires positive: it cannot cover both layers. Eliminating the vertical component gives the strict necessary angular condition |angle(e_j,-w)|<pi/2-pi/(2n), so one direction covers at most floor(n/2) top (or bottom) vertices. Conversely each consecutive block of <=floor(n/2) vertices admits a vertical parameter strictly between max(0,-c cos(alpha)+q sin(alpha)) and cos(alpha), producing one direction. Disjoint consecutive block partitions prove I=2ceil(n/floor(n/2)); cyclic maximal blocks weighted by 1/floor(n/2) per direction attain I*=2n/floor(n/2), matching vertex-sum lower bound. Vertex illumination implies face illumination since each face has fewer active facet constraints than an incident vertex. Independent facet-plane and constructed-block tests checked n=3,4,5,7,8,9,12 at two nonzero heights; the symbolic all-n cap and interval, not finite tests, establish universality.
residual_risks: Independent numerical checks cover only finitely many n and h; arbitrary n,h correctness relies on the explicit open-arc proof and sharp construction, not floating-point support checks.

value.rationale: Ordinary versus fractional illumination is an established convex-geometric covering invariant. The exact integral/fractional gap for a natural infinite family, abrupt even/odd dichotomy, and independence from positive aspect ratio provide meaningful structural information; no downstream theorem is necessary for this exact classification.
residual_risks: Novelty, correctness and reproducibility alone do not establish value; here the mathematical purpose and natural invariant are separately articulated.

final_claim: For every n>=3 and h>0, the directed ordinary illumination of the two half-step rotated regular n-gon antiprism is 4 for even n and 6 for odd n; its finite fractional illumination number is 2n/floor(n/2), independent of h.
limitations: No assertion that any particular optimizer is unique. The weighted definition uses finite nonnegative direction weights, not X-ray undirected lines.
Historical priority remains qualified; no publication attempt while public operational metadata is unsanitized.
